subject: GitHub app SSO + rate limits — demo request and prep
messages:
From: Marta Kowalski <marta@codemine.io>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 12 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: GitHub app SSO + rate limits — quick questions before demo

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the quick signup flow — we got a trial API key and played around with the hosted endpoints. CodeMine is evaluating Redwood for a couple of integration use cases: provisioning model inference for our CI pipelines and building a GitHub App to surface model suggestions in PRs. Before we jump into a demo, we have three quick questions to help us prep: 

1) SSO / SAML: we require SSO for installer flows. Does Redwood's GitHub App support SSO-managed installs (org-level SAML enforcement + SCIM provisioning)?

2) Rate limits: our CI runs make a burst of small requests across 40 runners. Do you expose per-token or per-org rate limit controls, and can we request higher burst capacity for scheduled CI windows?

3) Webhooks & SSH: for repos behind an enterprise SSH proxy we sometimes need to route webhooks through a proxy. Any constraints on webhook endpoints or recommendations for handling webhooks from private GHEs?

We can do a demo next week; available windows are Mon/Tue 9–11 PT or Wed afternoon PT. If useful, I attached a short repo-access token we can provide for a pre-call check.

Thanks — looking forward,

Marta
Marta Kowalski
Head of DevOps, CodeMine
M: +1 (415) 555-0172

Attachment: codemine-repo-access.txt (stub: readme of minimal scopes and a deploy key)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.inference>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.inference>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.inference>

Subject: Re: GitHub app SSO + rate limits — quick questions before demo

Hi Marta — great to hear from you and thanks for the context. I'm Naomi (SDR on the open-source/connector motion) — copying Aditya (your SDR) and Soojin (solutions engineering) so we can cover scheduling + technical prep.

Short answers upfront:
- SSO: yes, Redwood supports organization-level SSO enforcement for private deployments and can integrate with SAML/SCIM flows for user provisioning. For hosted customers we provide an SSO-enabled control plane option (we'll surface details in the call).
- Rate limits: we have per-API-key and per-org rate controls; for CI bursts we offer scheduled burst windows via Dedicated reservations or a temporary uplift for hosted customers (subject to capacity).
- Webhooks/SSH: private GHE behind a proxy is common — we support webhook relay patterns and can propose a lightweight relay agent. We'll ask a couple of network details in the pre-call.

Can we lock a 30-min demo on Monday 14 Dec at 9:30 PT? Aditya will send a calendar invite. For the technical pre-call, Soojin — can you look at the repo link and the repo-access stub Marta attached and share any preflight checks we want them to run? I've attached our standard precall checklist as a PDF to help the customer prepare.

Agenda for the 30-min session (high-level):
- 10m: Customer goals + repo/CI patterns
- 10m: Redwood demo (GitHub App install, SSO, webhook patterns)
- 10m: Next steps (evaluation plan, Dedicated vs hosted, PO/AP process)

Thanks — we'll get an invite over.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Development, Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.inference | +1 (650) 555-0119

- The Monday slot is great, but could we do 9:00 PT instead of 9:30? We have a tight backlog window.
- I've pasted the GitHub repo URL here (private): https://github.com/codemine/platform-service — we'll grant redwood-inference[bot] a read-only deploy key (see attached codemine-repo-access.txt).

Looking forward to the call.

—Marta

Hi Marta — Soojin from Solutions Engineering here. Thanks for the repo link and the details about the SSH proxy. A few practical items ahead of Monday's call (answers + preflight):

1) SSO / SAML: For Hosted customers we offer an SSO-enabled control plane that ties into your IdP (SAML) and we can enable SCIM for user provisioning. For Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) we can wire SCIM into your identity provider directly. On the call we'll want to capture: IdP type, attributes required on user objects, and SCIM endpoints.

2) Rate limiting & bursts: We recommend one of two approaches depending on expected token volume:
   - Short-term: request a hosted burst uplift (we can provision a temporary quota increase for scheduled CI windows).
   - Long-term: Dedicated reservation with scheduled autoscaling plus a burst policy.
We can supply a sample policy (JSON) during the call.

3) Webhook relay & SSH proxy pattern: Common pattern is to run a lightweight forwarder in the DMZ that accepts GHE webhooks and forwards to a public relay we manage (TLS + HMAC). We have a sample container manifest (small Go forwarder) and a k8s job for edge relay — I'll paste a link in our call notes. If you cannot run a relay, we can also accept signed webhook payloads via a mutual-TLS endpoint on a peered VPC for Private customers.

Preflight checklist (short list we like customers to run before the demo):
- Confirm read-only deploy key or repo invite for redwood-inference[bot] (we only need to scan bundles and config).
- Share a sample CI job that hits your GH runners (a short YAML snippet).
- List expected concurrency (runners x parallel jobs) and typical request size.

I attached a quick precall checklist and will drop the sample forwarder manifest into the calendar invite. For Monday, 9:00 PT works for us — Naomi, if you can update the invite to 09:00 we'll lock it.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0199
